question: For what does Paul thank God?
explanation: Paul thanks God for their fellowship in the gospel from the first day until now.

question: What is Paul confident God will do?
choices: Return him to Philippi at once
Perform the good work until the day of Jesus Christ
Make them leaders over all churches
explanation: Paul says God will complete the good work He began in them.

question: What had Paul's imprisonment actually helped do?
explanation: Paul explains that his imprisonment has served to advance the gospel.

question: What does Paul say about living and dying?
choices: To live is service, and to die is peace
To live is Christ, and to die is gain
To live is sacrifice, and to die is glory
explanation: Paul says, 'For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain.'

question: How are believers told to stand?
choices: In one spirit, with one mind striving together for the faith of the gospel
explanation: Paul calls them to stand fast in one spirit and strive together for the gospel.

question: What does Paul tell the Philippians to be?
explanation: Paul urges them to be likeminded, having the same love and one accord.

question: What attitude does Paul command?
choices: In lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves
explanation: Paul calls them to humility and to value others above themselves.

question: What form did Christ take?
explanation: Christ made Himself of no reputation and took the form of a servant.

question: What name has God exalted above every name?
explanation: God highly exalted Jesus so that every knee should bow at His name.

question: Whom does Paul hope to send shortly?
explanation: Paul says he hopes to send Timothy soon to learn how the Philippians are doing.

question: What does Paul tell the Philippians to do?
explanation: Paul begins the chapter by telling them to rejoice in the Lord.

question: How does Paul want to be found in Christ?
choices: Having the righteousness which is through faith in Christ
Having his own righteousness from the law
explanation: Paul wants the righteousness that comes through faith in Christ.

question: Toward what does Paul press?
choices: The mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus
explanation: Paul presses toward the mark for the heavenly prize in Christ.

question: Where does Paul say believers' citizenship is?
explanation: Paul reminds them that their citizenship is in heaven.

question: Which two women does Paul urge to be of the same mind?
explanation: Paul beseeches Euodias and Syntyche to be of the same mind in the Lord.

question: How often does Paul say to rejoice?
explanation: Paul says, 'Rejoice in the Lord alway: and again I say, Rejoice.'

question: What should believers do instead of being anxious?
explanation: They are to present their requests to God by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving.

question: What kinds of things are believers told to think on?
choices: Things that are true, honest, just, pure, lovely, and of good report
explanation: Paul tells them to focus their minds on what is virtuous and praiseworthy.

question: What famous statement does Paul make?
choices: I can overcome by my wisdom
I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me
I must finish the race alone
explanation: Paul says Christ gives him strength for all things.

question: Who is named with Paul at the start of the letter?
explanation: 'Paul and Timotheus, the servants of Jesus Christ.'

question: To the saints in which city is the letter written?
explanation: 'To all the saints in Christ Jesus which are at Philippi.'

question: With whom are the saints at Philippi addressed?
explanation: 'To all the saints... which are at Philippi, with the bishops and deacons.'

question: In what place had Paul's bonds become manifest?
explanation: 'My bonds in Christ are manifest in all the palace, and in all other places.'

question: Besides envy and strife, from what motive do some preach Christ?
explanation: 'Some indeed preach Christ even of envy and strife; and some also of good will.'

question: What does Paul say he rejoices in about the preaching?
explanation: 'Every way, whether in pretence, or in truth, Christ is preached; and I therein do rejoice.'

question: What does Paul say is 'far better' than staying in the flesh?
choices: To be set free from prison
To depart and be with Christ
explanation: 'Having a desire to depart, and to be with Christ; which is far better.'

question: Why does Paul say it is more needful to stay in the flesh?
choices: For his own work in prison
explanation: 'Nevertheless to abide in the flesh is more needful for you.'

question: What has been given to believers besides believing on Christ?
explanation: 'It is given in the behalf of Christ, not only to believe on him, but also to suffer for his sake.'

question: When does Paul thank his God for the Philippians?
choices: Only when they send a gift
explanation: 'I thank my God upon every remembrance of you.'

question: How does Paul make request in every prayer for the Philippians?
explanation: 'Always in every prayer of mine for you all making request with joy.'

question: Of what were the Philippians partakers in Paul's bonds?
explanation: 'Both in my bonds... ye all are partakers of my grace.'

question: Whom does Paul call as his record that he longs after them all?
explanation: 'God is my record, how greatly I long after you all.'

question: In what does Paul pray their love will abound more and more?
explanation: 'That your love may abound yet more and more in knowledge and in all judgment.'

question: What does Paul pray they may approve?
explanation: 'That ye may approve things that are excellent.'

question: With what does Paul pray they will be filled?
choices: The fruits of righteousness by Jesus Christ
explanation: 'Being filled with the fruits of righteousness, which are by Jesus Christ.'

question: What did many of the brethren do because of Paul's bonds?
choices: Became more bold to speak the word without fear
explanation: 'Many of the brethren... waxing confident by my bonds, are much more bold to speak the word without fear.'

question: Why do some preach Christ out of contention?
choices: To win honour from the rulers
Supposing to add affliction to Paul's bonds
explanation: They preach 'of contention, not sincerely, supposing to add affliction to my bonds.'

question: What do those who preach of love know?
choices: That Paul is set for the defence of the gospel
That Paul will soon be freed
That Paul is the chief apostle
explanation: 'The other of love, knowing that I am set for the defence of the gospel.'

question: Through what does Paul know his situation will turn to his salvation?
choices: Through the work of the bishops
Through the gifts of the saints
Through the Philippians' prayer and the supply of the Spirit
explanation: 'This shall turn to my salvation through your prayer, and the supply of the Spirit of Jesus Christ.'

question: What is Paul's earnest expectation and hope?
choices: That he will be freed within the year
That he will see Philippi again
That in nothing he shall be ashamed
That he will rule with Christ
explanation: 'That in nothing I shall be ashamed, but that with all boldness... Christ shall be magnified in my body.'

question: What does Paul say he knows about his future with them?
choices: That he shall be put to death
That he shall abide and continue with them all
That he shall go to Spain
That he shall never see them
explanation: 'I know that I shall abide and continue with you all.'

question: What will Paul's coming to them again make more abundant?
explanation: 'That your rejoicing may be more abundant in Jesus Christ for me by my coming to you again.'

question: How are the Philippians told to face their adversaries?
explanation: 'And in nothing terrified by your adversaries.'

question: To their adversaries, the Philippians' fearlessness is an evident token of what?
explanation: 'An evident token of perdition, but to you of salvation, and that of God.'

question: What does Paul say the Philippians share with him in the conflict?
choices: The same conflict they saw in him and now hear to be in him
explanation: 'Having the same conflict which ye saw in me, and now hear to be in me.'

question: Besides his bonds, in what were the Philippians partakers of Paul's grace?
choices: The defence and confirmation of the gospel
explanation: 'In the defence and confirmation of the gospel, ye all are partakers of my grace.'

question: Paul prays they may be sincere and without offence until when?
explanation: 'That ye may be sincere and without offence till the day of Christ.'

question: To whose glory and praise are the fruits of righteousness?
explanation: The fruits of righteousness are 'unto the glory and praise of God.'

question: Between life and death, what does Paul say he does not know?
explanation: 'Yet what I shall choose I wot not.'

question: In what two ways does Paul say Christ is preached?
explanation: 'Whether in pretence, or in truth, Christ is preached.'

question: What must be 'as it becometh the gospel of Christ'?
explanation: 'Only let your conversation be as it becometh the gospel of Christ.'

question: How does Paul describe those who preach Christ of contention?
explanation: 'The one preach Christ of contention, not sincerely.'

question: How does Paul expect Christ to be magnified in his body?
explanation: 'With all boldness, as always, so now also Christ shall be magnified in my body.'

question: From whom does Paul wish grace and peace?
choices: God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ
explanation: 'Grace be unto you, and peace, from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.'

question: What reason does Paul give for thinking well of them all?
choices: They have sent him a gift
He has them in his heart
explanation: 'It is meet for me to think this of you all, because I have you in my heart.'

question: Whose Spirit does Paul say will supply him?
explanation: 'The supply of the Spirit of Jesus Christ.'

question: Paul says the salvation shown by their fearlessness is of whom?
explanation: 'To them an evident token of perdition, but to you of salvation, and that of God.'

question: For what purpose does Paul say he will continue with them?
choices: Their furtherance and joy of faith
explanation: 'I shall abide and continue with you all for your furtherance and joy of faith.'

question: What do Paul and Timotheus call themselves?
explanation: 'Paul and Timotheus, the servants of Jesus Christ.'

question: Unto what death did Christ become obedient?
explanation: He 'became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross.'

question: What shall every tongue confess about Jesus Christ?
choices: That he is the king of the Jews
explanation: 'Every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord.'

question: To the glory of whom do tongues confess that Jesus is Lord?
explanation: 'To the glory of God the Father.'

question: Whom does Paul call 'my brother, and companion in labour'?
explanation: 'Epaphroditus, my brother, and companion in labour, and fellow soldier.'

question: What happened to Epaphroditus?
choices: He was beaten by a crowd
He was sick nigh unto death
explanation: 'For indeed he was sick nigh unto death.'

question: Who had mercy on Epaphroditus?
explanation: 'But God had mercy on him; and not on him only, but on me also.'

question: As what do the Philippians shine in the world?
explanation: 'Among whom ye shine as lights in the world.'

question: What are the Philippians told to do without?
explanation: 'Do all things without murmurings and disputings.'

question: With what are they told to work out their own salvation?
explanation: 'Work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.'

question: Who worketh in believers both to will and to do?
explanation: 'It is God which worketh in you both to will and to do of his good pleasure.'

question: Through what is nothing to be done?
explanation: 'Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory.'

question: On whose things are believers told to look, as well as their own?
explanation: 'Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others.'

question: Being in the form of God, Christ thought it not robbery to be what?
explanation: 'Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God.'

question: In whose likeness was Christ made?
explanation: He 'was made in the likeness of men.'

question: Of what places does Paul say every knee shall bow?
choices: Heaven, earth and under the earth
The temple, the city and the field
explanation: 'Of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth.'

question: Being found in fashion as a man, what did Christ do?
explanation: 'Being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself.'

question: Obeying not only in his presence, how does Paul say they should obey now?
explanation: 'As ye have always obeyed, not as in my presence only, but now much more in my absence.'

question: Without murmuring they will be blameless and harmless, the what of God?
explanation: 'That ye may be blameless and harmless, the sons of God.'

question: In the midst of what kind of nation do they shine?
explanation: 'In the midst of a crooked and perverse nation.'

question: What are they to hold forth?
explanation: 'Holding forth the word of life.'

question: What does Paul want to be able to say in the day of Christ?
choices: That he has finished the temple
That he has not run in vain
explanation: 'That I may rejoice in the day of Christ, that I have not run in vain, neither laboured in vain.'

question: What does Paul ask the Philippians to do for the same cause?
explanation: 'For the same cause also do ye joy, and rejoice with me.'

question: Why does Paul hope to send Timotheus to them?
choices: That he may be of good comfort when he knows their state
That the church may collect a gift
That the bishops may be appointed
explanation: 'That I also may be of good comfort, when I know your state.'

question: What does Paul say of Timotheus compared with others?
choices: He is the oldest of the apostles
He is the best teacher of the law
He is the most feared by Rome
He has no one likeminded to naturally care for them
explanation: 'I have no man likeminded, who will naturally care for your state.'

question: How has Timotheus served with Paul in the gospel?
choices: As a slave with his master
As a soldier with his captain
As a son with the father
As a scribe with a prophet
explanation: 'As a son with the father, he hath served with me in the gospel.'

question: What does Paul say 'all seek'?
choices: Their own, not the things of Jesus Christ
explanation: 'All seek their own, not the things which are Jesus Christ's.'

question: When does Paul hope to send Timotheus?
choices: As soon as he sees how it will go with him
explanation: 'Him therefore I hope to send presently, so soon as I shall see how it will go with me.'

question: What does Paul trust the Lord he himself will do?
explanation: 'I trust in the Lord that I also myself shall come shortly.'

question: Why was Epaphroditus full of heaviness?
choices: He had been parted from Paul
The Philippians had heard that he had been sick
explanation: 'He longed after you all, and was full of heaviness, because that ye had heard that he had been sick.'

question: Why does Paul say God's mercy on Epaphroditus was also mercy on him?
choices: Lest he be left alone in prison
Lest he should have sorrow upon sorrow
explanation: 'Not on him only, but on me also, lest I should have sorrow upon sorrow.'

question: Why did Paul send Epaphroditus the more carefully?
choices: That they may rejoice and he be the less sorrowful
That the church might be warned
That the gift might be returned
explanation: 'That, when ye see him again, ye may rejoice, and that I may be the less sorrowful.'

question: How are they told to receive Epaphroditus?
choices: In the Lord with all gladness
explanation: 'Receive him therefore in the Lord with all gladness; and hold such in reputation.'

question: Why was Epaphroditus nigh unto death?
choices: For Christ's work, to supply their lack of service
explanation: 'For the work of Christ he was nigh unto death... to supply your lack of service toward me.'

question: What role does Paul give Epaphroditus toward the Philippians?
choices: Their messenger, who ministered to Paul's wants
explanation: 'Your messenger, and he that ministered to my wants.'

question: Which of these does Paul list in his appeal beginning 'if any'?
explanation: 'If any comfort of love, if any fellowship of the Spirit.'

question: Upon what does Paul say he may be offered?
choices: The sacrifice and service of their faith
explanation: 'If I be offered upon the sacrifice and service of your faith, I joy, and rejoice with you all.'

question: Besides brother and companion in labour, what does Paul call Epaphroditus?
explanation: 'Epaphroditus, my brother, and companion in labour, and fellow soldier.'

question: Whose proof, Paul says, do the Philippians know?
explanation: 'Ye know the proof of him, that, as a son with the father, he hath served with me.'

question: In whom does Paul trust to send Timotheus?
explanation: 'I trust in the Lord Jesus to send Timotheus shortly unto you.'

question: According to what does God work in believers to will and to do?
explanation: 'It is God which worketh in you both to will and to do of his good pleasure.'

question: On which day was Paul circumcised?
explanation: Paul was 'circumcised the eighth day.'

question: Of which tribe was Paul?
explanation: 'Of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin.'

question: As touching the law, what was Paul?
explanation: 'As touching the law, a Pharisee.'

question: Concerning zeal, what had Paul done?
explanation: 'Concerning zeal, persecuting the church.'

question: For whose sake did Paul count his gains as loss?
explanation: 'What things were gain to me, those I counted loss for Christ.'

question: Of which of these does Paul say 'Beware'?
explanation: 'Beware of dogs, beware of evil workers, beware of the concision.'

question: What will Christ do for our vile body?
choices: Change it to be like his glorious body
explanation: He 'shall change our vile body, that it may be fashioned like unto his glorious body.'

question: What does Paul say writing the same things is for them?
explanation: 'To write the same things to you, to me indeed is not grievous, but for you it is safe.'

question: We who worship God in the spirit have no what?
explanation: 'We are the circumcision, which worship God in the spirit... and have no confidence in the flesh.'

question: How does Paul describe his Hebrew standing?
explanation: 'An Hebrew of the Hebrews.'

question: Touching the righteousness in the law, what was Paul?
explanation: 'Touching the righteousness which is in the law, blameless.'

question: What does Paul say he wants to win?
explanation: 'That I may win Christ.'

question: Besides knowing Christ, what does Paul want to know?
explanation: 'That I may know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings.'

question: What does Paul do with the things which are behind?
explanation: 'Forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before.'

question: How does Paul say he stands regarding being perfect?
choices: He has not already attained or been made perfect
He has no wish to be perfect
explanation: 'Not as though I had already attained, either were already perfect.'

question: Of those who are enemies of the cross, whose God is what?
explanation: 'Whose God is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things.'

question: What is the end of those enemies of the cross?
explanation: 'Whose end is destruction.'

question: How does Paul tell of the enemies of the cross?
explanation: 'I have told you often, and now tell you even weeping.'

question: For the excellency of what does Paul count all things but loss?
choices: The knowledge of Christ Jesus his Lord
explanation: 'I count all things but loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord.'

question: What does Paul say he counts the things he lost?
explanation: 'Do count them but dung, that I may win Christ.'

question: What does Paul hope, by any means, to attain?
explanation: 'If by any means I might attain unto the resurrection of the dead.'

question: For whom does Paul say he is apprehended?
explanation: 'That I may apprehend that for which also I am apprehended of Christ Jesus.'

question: What does Paul tell the brethren to do about those who walk as he does?
choices: Be followers together of him and mark them
explanation: 'Be followers together of me, and mark them which walk so as ye have us for an ensample.'

question: If any are otherwise minded, what does Paul say God will do?
explanation: 'If in any thing ye be otherwise minded, God shall reveal even this unto you.'

question: By what working can Christ change our vile body?
choices: The working of the Spirit in the church
The working by which he subdues all things to himself
explanation: 'According to the working whereby he is able even to subdue all things unto himself.'

question: How does Paul compare himself with any who trust in the flesh?
explanation: 'If any other man thinketh that he hath whereof he might trust in the flesh, I more.'

question: To what does Paul want to be made conformable?
explanation: 'Being made conformable unto his death.'

question: Of what stock was Paul?
explanation: 'Of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin.'

question: Whom does Paul call 'the circumcision'?
choices: Those who worship God in the spirit and rejoice in Christ
explanation: 'We are the circumcision, which worship God in the spirit, and rejoice in Christ Jesus.'

question: Whom does Paul call his joy and crown?
explanation: 'My brethren dearly beloved and longed for, my joy and crown.'

question: What will keep the hearts and minds of believers through Christ Jesus?
choices: The peace of God, which passeth all understanding
explanation: 'The peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.'

question: In whatever state he is, what has Paul learned to be?
explanation: 'I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content.'

question: According to what will God supply all their need?
choices: His riches in glory by Christ Jesus
explanation: 'My God shall supply all your need according to his riches in glory by Christ Jesus.'

question: Who brought Paul the things sent from Philippi?
explanation: 'Having received of Epaphroditus the things which were sent from you.'

question: Chiefly which saints salute them?
explanation: 'All the saints salute you, chiefly they that are of Caesar's household.'

question: In which city did the Philippians send help to Paul more than once?
explanation: 'Even in Thessalonica ye sent once and again unto my necessity.'

question: Why did Paul rejoice greatly in the Lord?
choices: Their care of him had flourished again
explanation: 'Now at the last your care of me hath flourished again.'

question: What had the Philippians lacked in caring for Paul?
explanation: 'Wherein ye were also careful, but ye lacked opportunity.'

question: Which pair of conditions has Paul been instructed to bear?
choices: To be free and to be bound
To be young and to be old
To be full and to be hungry
To be near and to be far
explanation: 'I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need.'

question: Which pair does Paul say he knows how to live through?
choices: To be praised and to be shamed
To be abased and to abound
To be sick and to be well
To be alone and to be with friends
explanation: 'I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound.'

question: What had the Philippians done with Paul's affliction?
choices: Sent word of it to Rome
explanation: 'Ye have well done, that ye did communicate with my affliction.'

question: What does Paul say he desires, rather than a gift?
choices: Fruit that may abound to their account
explanation: 'Not because I desire a gift: but I desire fruit that may abound to your account.'

question: How does Paul describe the gift to God?
choices: A tithe of the first fruits
A sweet-smelling odour, a sacrifice acceptable to God
explanation: 'An odour of a sweet smell, a sacrifice acceptable, wellpleasing to God.'

question: How does Paul say he stands after receiving the gift?
choices: He has all and abounds, and is full
He is in debt to them
explanation: 'But I have all, and abound: I am full.'

question: What reason does Paul give after 'Let your moderation be known unto all men'?
explanation: 'Let your moderation be known unto all men. The Lord is at hand.'

question: Who will be with those who do the things they learned and saw in Paul?
explanation: 'Those things... do: and the God of peace shall be with you.'

question: When Paul left Macedonia, how many churches shared with him in giving and receiving?
explanation: No church communicated with Paul in giving and receiving, 'but ye only.'

question: Whom does Paul ask the true yokefellow to help?
choices: Those women who laboured with him in the gospel
explanation: 'Help those women which laboured with me in the gospel.'

question: Which man is named with the women whom the yokefellow is asked to help?
explanation: 'With Clement also, and with other my fellowlabourers.'

question: Whose names are in the book of life?
explanation: 'With other my fellowlabourers, whose names are in the book of life.'

question: Which of these is named among the things to think on?
explanation: 'Whatsoever things are true, honest, just, pure, lovely, of good report.'

question: From where had Paul departed when no church but theirs shared with him?
explanation: 'When I departed from Macedonia, no church communicated with me... but ye only.'

question: Whom does Paul tell them to salute?
explanation: 'Salute every saint in Christ Jesus.'

question: Who greet the Philippians, besides all the saints?
explanation: 'The brethren which are with me greet you.'

question: To whom does Paul give glory for ever and ever?
explanation: 'Now unto God and our Father be glory for ever and ever. Amen.'

question: Whose grace does Paul close the letter with?
explanation: 'The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all.'

question: In whom does Paul tell them to stand fast?
explanation: 'So stand fast in the Lord, my dearly beloved.'

question: What does Paul say should be known unto all men?
explanation: 'Let your moderation be known unto all men.'

question: In what did the women labour with Paul?
explanation: 'Those women which laboured with me in the gospel.'

question: Paul says he does not speak 'in respect of' what?
explanation: 'Not that I speak in respect of want.'
